e7ab27a187.q: What caused multifamily deals to fail during the 2022-2025 market downturn despite prior success?
e7ab27a187.a: Interest rates on floating-rate bridge debt went from 4% to 10-11% between 2022 and 2023, while rents stagnated or declined and tenants fell behind on payments. Insurance costs spiked dramatically—Florida saw 200-300% increases, and one South Texas property went from 1.2 to 3.6 million annually. Combined with massive oversupply in multifamily and properties worth far less than their loan balances, operators had to choose between throwing capital at deals to extend runway or handing back keys to lenders, with many finding that even 12-24 month loan modifications proved insufficient.

74e63c5dec.q: What property tax assessment shock did Think Multifamily experience and how did it impact deal feasibility?
74e63c5dec.a: One Think Multifamily property valued around 10 million had its property tax assessment frozen for four years, then the county tried to raise it to 21 million in a single year with no logical support. Lenders often require escrow of the full disputed amount even during appeals, forcing operators to tie up capital on uncertain liabilities. This unpredictability—varying significantly by county—became a critical factor in underwriting and deal viability.

57a0839e2a.q: How did cap rate expansion from 2022 to 2024 make it impossible to sell properties at loan payoff?
57a0839e2a.a: In parts of Florida, cap rates expanded from 4.4% in 2022 to 7.5% by 2024, leaving properties completely underwater relative to their loan balances. Properties that brokers valued at 9-10 million prior to 2022 were receiving offers at 17 million or less by 2023-2024, making it impossible to sell and pay off the loan with any remaining equity or proceeds.

bf735001b6.q: What is the required cash-on-cash return for multifamily deals to attract capital in the current market environment?
bf735001b6.a: In the current environment with risk-free CDs yielding 5% or higher, investors expect cash-on-cash returns close to that risk-free alternative to justify equity investment. If multifamily deals cannot deliver cash-on-cash yields competitive with liquid risk-free investments, it becomes very difficult to raise capital, even accounting for tax benefits and long-term appreciation.
